subject: Housing Home Rule Petitions and Funding
overview: Councilor Matt Leming recapped current and upcoming housing policy initiatives, focusing on home rule petitions for rent stabilization and real estate transfer fees. The proposals seek to provide the city with new mechanisms to fund the Affordable Housing Trust and address local housing affordability.

items.title: Rent Stabilization Home Rule Petition
items.summary: Discussed a home rule petition for rent stabilization that would seek state authority to cap annual rent increases at 5%.

items.title: Real Estate Transfer Fee Home Rule Petition
items.summary: Tabled a home rule petition proposing a 2% tax on home sales over $1 million to fund the Affordable Housing Trust until the March 12 meeting. The proposal includes specific exemptions for vulnerable seniors and property transfers between family members.

items.title: Loughlin Court Redevelopment
items.summary: Approved final zoning for the Loughlin Court redevelopment, a project costing over $100 million funded primarily by state and federal grants. The city contributed $2.4 million toward the project from Community Preservation Act funds.

items.title: Developer Linkage Fees Resolution
items.summary: Announced a forthcoming resolution to update developer linkage fees, which have not been adjusted since the 1990s. The update would direct a portion of developer fees into the Affordable Housing Trust to support local development projects.
